title: Chinese Carmakers Try to Break Free from the CATL Herd - The Wire China
gist: Chinese carmakers, after four years of a price war, are turning on battery giant CATL, which has absorbed much of the auto sector's profits, by moving to lower-tier suppliers or in-house batteries. Only the teaser is available (paywalled).

insights.claim: Four years into a vicious price war, the Chinese EV industry has turned its focus on CATL as a new target for cost reduction.
insights.speaker: Ella Apostoaie
insights.so_what: Margin pressure is migrating up the supply chain to battery makers; watch CATL pricing power.

insights.claim: CATL has long dominated the car battery market and absorbed much of the Chinese auto sector's profits.
insights.speaker: Ella Apostoaie
insights.so_what: CATL's profit share is the pool carmakers are trying to recapture.

insights.claim: A growing number of Chinese carmakers, from Li Auto to Xiaomi, are shifting to lower-tier battery suppliers or designing their own batteries.
insights.speaker: Ella Apostoaie
insights.so_what: Supplier diversification and vertical integration are a risk to CATL's share and a tailwind for second-tier battery makers.
